title: Public policy: editorial notes and questions
summary: Read the surrounding notes and questions alongside the principal cases. The complete assigned pages are preserved here.
notes:
Blossom Farm Products Co. v. Kasson Cheese Co., Inc.: Blossom shows that formation and performance do not end the enforceability inquiry. A court must also consider the relationship between the requested judgment and public policies implicated by the transaction.

X.L.O. Concrete Corp. v. Rivergate Corp.: Compare Blossom Farm to see why “connected to illegality” is an insufficient rule. The relationship between the specific performance sought, the prohibited conduct, and the parties’ relative positions must be explained.

Hassler v. Circle C Resources: Hassler links the substantive limits on a restraint to the remedy for excessive drafting. The choice between rewriting and nonenforcement changes the incentives created by the rule.
